title: AI, Algorithms, and Misinformation
bookshelves: Category: Reference, Information and Interdisciplinary subjects
Category: Economics, Finance, Business and Management
summary: This book examines how - in the 21st century world of big data and social media - artificial intelligence and algorithms are being used to predict our economic, political, and cultural activity. Drawing inspiration from the concept of a "minority report," as introduced in Philip K. Dick’s 1956 short story, the book explores how the byproduct of digital content on social media often generates a collective perception of reality. This book breaks down how this collective perception is ultimately manufactured by cultural, political, and economic interests, and how additional issues - such as data errors, misinformation, and bias - can often render it false. Applying critical political economic analysis and cultural legal studies to these problems, Blevins emphasizes how we can do more to challenge the perceptions that pervade popular online discourse. Throughout the book, he demystifies the systems and processes that generate these information flows, enabling readers to better fight for remedies to the problem - legal and otherwise - and create a more just digital future. This book will be of interest to students and scholars of media and communication studies, political science, sociology, and beyond who have an interest in understanding and addressing the impact AI, algorithms, and misinformation have on social media and society.
